The biggest tradeoff is between **growth and housing costs**. Texas and North Carolina are both growing and had positive net migration in 2024, while New York’s population was nearly flat from 2020 to 2025 and its net migration was negative.

Texas is the largest and fastest-growing of the three by population: it reached about **31.7 million in 2025**, up **8.5% since 2020**. North Carolina reached **11.2 million**, up **7.2%**, while New York was essentially unchanged at **20.0 million**, down **0.6%** since 2020. The migration figures point in the same direction: Texas gained **72,680** people through net migration in 2024, North Carolina gained **58,610**, and New York lost **130,436**. These figures describe movement patterns, not the reasons behind them.

On the supplied 2024 housing measures, **North Carolina has the lowest median rent** at **$1,338**, followed by Texas at **$1,475** and New York at **$1,634**. Texas has the lowest median home value, at **$313,200**, compared with **$333,000** in North Carolina and **$449,800** in New York. New York does have the highest median household income—**$85,820**, versus **$79,721** in Texas and **$73,958** in North Carolina—but its housing costs are also higher on these measures.

The education picture is more mixed. North Carolina has the highest share of adults with at least a high school education (**90.1%**), while New York leads in bachelor’s-degree attainment (**40.2%**). North Carolina is next at **35.7%**, and Texas at **33.8%**. In the supplied assessment scores, North Carolina has the highest math score (**276**), while New York has the highest reading score (**257**); these are 2024 figures and do not by themselves establish an overall education ranking.

In short, **Texas** combines the largest scale, strongest population growth, and lower median home values than the other two, but has the lowest supplied educational-attainment measures. **North Carolina** pairs strong growth with the lowest median rent and the strongest high-school and math figures. **New York** has the highest income and bachelor’s attainment, but also the highest housing costs and substantial net outmigration.
